questions.text: Which databases are created when a new PostgreSQL cluster is initialized?

answers.text: postgres, template0, and template1
postgres, public, and template1
postgres, pg_catalog, and template0
Only postgres

questions.explanation: Cluster initialization creates three databases: postgres, template0, and template1. Other databases are subsequently created by cloning an existing database.

questions.text: Which statements about the cluster's standard databases are correct? Select all that apply.

answers.text: template1 is used by default as the template for new databases
template0 should normally be kept free of user changes
The postgres database is used as the default database for connections
Every new database is necessarily created empty and never uses a template

questions.explanation: template1 is the standard CREATE DATABASE template, template0 is kept as a clean original template, and postgres is intended, among other uses, for normal connections to the cluster.

source.locator: Slide 3, purpose of postgres, template0, and template1

questions.text: What does CREATE DATABASE actually do when no template database is specified explicitly?

answers.text: Copies template1
Copies postgres
Copies template0
Creates a completely empty file structure without system objects

questions.explanation: CREATE DATABASE is implemented as a copy of an existing database. The default template is template1.

source.locator: Section 23.3, template1 as the default template

questions.text: When is using template0 especially appropriate? Select all that apply.

answers.text: When restoring a database from a pg_dump into a clean database
When creating a database with encoding or locale settings different from template1
When a database without user objects added to template1 is required
When all local additions from template1 must be copied automatically

questions.explanation: template0 preserves the original contents and provides a clean database. This is useful for dump restoration and for creating a database with different encoding and locale settings.

questions.text: What happens if you try to clone a database while active connections to the source database remain?

answers.text: CREATE DATABASE fails with an error
Active connections are automatically moved to the new database
Only system objects are copied
PostgreSQL automatically COMMITs every connection and continues copying

questions.explanation: To copy a template database, existing connections to it must be closed. If other sessions are connected, CREATE DATABASE reports an error.

source.locator: Section 23.3, restrictions when copying a database

questions.text: What purposes do PostgreSQL schemas serve? Select all that apply.

answers.text: They create namespaces for objects inside a database
They allow objects to be grouped logically
They allow objects with the same name to exist in different schemas
They allow one SQL session to connect to multiple cluster databases at once

questions.explanation: A schema is a namespace inside one database. It is used to organize objects logically and prevent name conflicts.

questions.text: How many cluster databases is an ordinary client session connected to at one time?

answers.text: One database
All databases in the cluster
template1 and one user database at the same time
One database for each schema being used

questions.explanation: A client connects to one database but can access objects in different schemas within it.

source.locator: Slide 6, client connection to a database

questions.text: Which statements about search_path are correct? Select all that apply.

answers.text: It defines the lookup order for objects referenced without a schema name
Schemas are searched in the order defined by the search path
Schemas that do not exist or are not accessible to the user can be omitted from the effective path
It can search for an object in another database of the cluster

questions.explanation: search_path applies to schemas of the current database. For an unqualified name, PostgreSQL searches objects through accessible schemas in the effective path in order.

questions.text: In which schema is a table created by CREATE TABLE t(...) when no schema is specified explicitly?

answers.text: The first suitable schema in the search path
Always pg_catalog
Always template1
A randomly selected accessible schema

questions.explanation: If a creation command does not contain a qualified name, PostgreSQL uses the first schema in search_path that is suitable for object creation.

source.locator: Section 5.9.3, current schema and object creation

questions.text: What does the default value search_path = "$user", public mean? Select all that apply.

answers.text: $user means a schema named after the current user, if such an accessible schema exists
public is considered after the user schema
If the user-named schema does not exist, that path element is ignored
$user means the operating-system user that runs the server

questions.explanation: The default search_path is "$user", public. The special $user component substitutes the current user name when a corresponding accessible schema exists.

questions.text: How does PostgreSQL determine the schema for the name app.orders?

answers.text: It uses the explicitly specified app schema and does not search for orders in the other search_path schemas
It first searches for orders in public
It first searches for orders in pg_catalog
It selects the first schema containing a table named orders regardless of app

questions.explanation: A name of the form schema.object is qualified: the schema is selected directly by that qualifier.

questions.text: Which statements about the special system-catalog schemas are correct? Select all that apply.

answers.text: pg_catalog contains system catalog objects
The system catalog contains metadata about PostgreSQL objects
information_schema provides a standardized SQL representation of metadata
public is a physical copy of pg_catalog

questions.explanation: pg_catalog contains PostgreSQL system catalogs, while information_schema provides another, standardized SQL representation of metadata.

questions.text: What happens to pg_catalog if that schema is not explicitly present in search_path?

answers.text: It is implicitly searched before explicitly listed ordinary schemas
System objects become inaccessible
It is automatically appended at the end
PostgreSQL replaces it with information_schema

questions.explanation: pg_catalog always participates in name lookup. If it is not listed explicitly, PostgreSQL searches it before ordinary path elements.

questions.text: Which statements about PostgreSQL temporary tables are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: They can exist only for a session or transaction
Their changes are not WAL-logged in the normal way
Their pages are not placed in the shared buffer cache
After a crash they are recovered together with permanent tables

questions.explanation: Temporary tables have session or transaction lifetime. They do not need crash recovery and use local temporary buffers of the backend process instead of the shared buffer cache.

questions.text: What does the name pg_temp mean in the current session?

answers.text: An alias for the current session's concrete temporary schema pg_temp_N
An alias for the public schema
The name of a cluster-wide temporary database
A synonym for the pg_wal directory

questions.explanation: The actual temporary schema has a name such as pg_temp_N. The universal name pg_temp refers to the temporary schema of the current session.

questions.text: Which statements about the current session's temporary schema are correct? Select all that apply.

answers.text: If pg_temp is not listed in search_path, it is implicitly considered before the other schemas
Objects in the temporary schema are removed when the session ends
PostgreSQL may retain the physical schema for reuse by later sessions
All sessions use the same temporary tables simultaneously through pg_temp

questions.explanation: Each session gets its own temporary schema. The pg_temp alias resolves to it; objects are removed at session end, while the schema itself can be reused.

questions.text: How can you obtain the effective search path including implicitly added schemas?

answers.text: current_schemas(true)
current_database(true)
pg_schema_path()
SHOW current_schema

questions.explanation: The material separately notes that the configured search_path value and the effective path can differ. current_schemas(true) shows the path including implicit schemas.

questions.text: Which schema privileges have the stated purpose? Select all that apply.

answers.text: USAGE allows access to objects in the schema when the required privileges on those objects are also present
CREATE allows new objects to be created in the schema
USAGE alone does not automatically grant all privileges on tables in the schema
CREATE on a schema automatically grants permission to modify every existing table in that schema

questions.explanation: Schema privileges and privileges on objects inside the schema are separate. USAGE allows use of the namespace, while CREATE allows object creation; privileges on individual tables and other objects are granted separately.

questions.text: How can a configuration parameter be set so that its default value applies to new sessions of a specific database?

answers.text: ALTER DATABASE name SET parameter TO value
ALTER SCHEMA name SET parameter TO value
CREATE DATABASE name WITH SESSION parameter
SET DATABASE parameter TO value

questions.explanation: ALTER DATABASE ... SET defines a default session value for a parameter at the level of a specific database. It takes effect for new connections.

questions.text: Which statements about temp_buffers are correct? Select all that apply.

answers.text: It sets the maximum amount of memory for temporary buffers in one session
These buffers are used only for temporary tables
The PostgreSQL 16 default is 8 MB
temp_buffers is one shared global memory pool for all server sessions

questions.explanation: temp_buffers is configured per session and applies to buffers for temporary tables. In PostgreSQL 16 the default is 8 MB.

questions.text: If the default temp_buffers value is 8MB, which value is four times larger?

answers.text: 32MB
16MB
64MB
4MB

questions.explanation: The default temp_buffers value is 8 MB. Four times that value is 32 MB; it can be set for a database with ALTER DATABASE ... SET.

source.locator: Slide 15, temp_buffers four times the default

questions.text: A database has schemas app and a schema named after the current user. Tables in both schemas must be accessible without qualification, with the user schema taking priority. Which actions satisfy this requirement? Select all that apply.

answers.text: Place the user schema before app in search_path
Include both schemas in search_path
If both schemas contain a table with the same name, the table in the earlier schema in search_path is found
Place app first so that the user schema has higher priority

questions.explanation: For an unqualified name, schemas are searched from left to right. Therefore the user schema must precede app to have higher priority.

source.locator: Slide 14, configuring the search path for two schemas

questions.text: What is the postgres.bki file used for during PostgreSQL bootstrap?

answers.text: It contains commands and initial data used by the server to create and initially populate the system catalogs
It stores WAL records of unfinished transactions
It contains user search_path settings
It is the cluster users' password file

questions.explanation: The documentation describes postgres.bki as a bootstrap file from which the server obtains commands and initial data used to build the system catalogs during initialization.

questions.text: Which statements about template databases and pg_database flags are correct? Select all that apply.

answers.text: datistemplate indicates whether the database may be used as a generally available template by users with CREATEDB
datallowconn controls whether new connections to the database are allowed
New connections to template0 are normally disabled to reduce the risk of modifying it
datallowconn = false automatically removes all already-open sessions

questions.explanation: In pg_database, datistemplate and datallowconn are used to manage template databases. Clearing datallowconn prevents new connections but does not itself terminate existing ones.
